- Build a complete, playable browser game based on “Gridiron Glory: The Road to Stardom,” with a football field game loop and a persistent single-player career.

## Requirements
- Create a mobile- and PC-friendly football game with 11-on-11 play, controls, practice, progression, position changes, name-seeded attributes, and earned nicknames.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Save a small JPEG screenshot for checks and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with localStorage career saves.
- Used fictional career scrimmages with Chicago Bears/Green Bay Packers team references; the UI notes that players and rosters are simulated, not current licensed rosters.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the main dashboard, career/player/practice modals, controls, responsive styling, name-seeded attributes, nickname logic, and local career progression.
- Added the football field canvas engine and adjusted its pointer/Space handling so play starts from the game UI rather than accidental canvas clicks.

### Active
- Validate the game in a browser, exercise play/practice/career flows, fix any issues, and save/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.
- Changes are uncommitted.

2. Check for browser console errors and test controls, play completion, practice, player editing, and career advancement.
3. Save a JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only that latest screenshot.
4. Report completed work and the simulated-roster assumption.

- `index.html`: Game dashboard and UI structure.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and touch controls.
- `app.js`: Career state, UI interactions, attributes, nicknames, and progression.
- `field.js`: Canvas football field, players, input, and play callbacks.

- The original game prompt’s final practice section ends mid-sentence after “unlocks Skill”; the implementation uses reasonable career/practice assumptions.

- `node --check app.js && node --check field.js` passed before the final field engine edits; rerun checks after changes.

## Objective
- Complete and validate a playable browser football game with an 11-on-11 field loop and persistent single-player career progression.

## Requirements
- Support mobile and PC, practice and progression, position changes, name-seeded attributes, and earned nicknames.
- Make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot; inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built as a standalone vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with localStorage saves.
- Career scrimmages reference fictionalized Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers teams; UI clarifies players and rosters are simulated, not current licensed rosters.
- The source prompt ended mid-sentence after “unlocks Skill”; implementation uses reasonable career and practice assumptions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the dashboard, career/player/practice modals, controls, responsive styling, name-seeded attributes, nickname logic, and local career progression.
- Implemented the canvas football field and adjusted input handling so plays start from the game UI.
- Ran `node --check app.js && node --check field.js` successfully before browser testing.
- Opened the game in Playwright and verified a play resolves, practice increases an attribute, and the player-edit modal opens.

### Active
- Continue browser validation of game controls, play completion, career advancement, player editing, and responsive layout.
- Save and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser checks from the currently open player-edit modal; verify saving a changed name/position and career advancement.
2. Check keyboard/touch controls and review browser console; a favicon request currently returns 404.
3. Save a JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only that latest screenshot.
4. Rerun JavaScript syntax checks and report results, including the simulated-roster assumption.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Dashboard and UI structure.
- `style.css`: Responsive styling and touch controls.
- `app.js`: Career state, UI interactions, attributes, nicknames, and progression.
- `field.js`: Canvas football field, players, input, and play callbacks.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are currently untracked.
- Browser validation produced one console error: `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found) @ http://localhost:3000/favicon.ico:0`.
- Browser state has one practice completed and one play resolved; the player-edit modal is open.
